platform.name: 2 Page Display for CHIP-8
platform.description: Andy Modla and Jef Winsor's 64x64 mode for CHIP-8 on the Cosmac VIP, using two pages of display memory (VIPER volume 1 issue 3, pp. 10-12). It patches the interpreter, and every program includes a machine-code patch at 0x200-0x249: the first instruction (1260) jumps over it, and the CHIP-8 program starts at 0x260. 0230 calls the patch's routine that clears both pages (the whole 64x64 screen). The known ROMs (kripod/chip8-roms' hires folder) also patch the interpreter themselves, so they run on an unmodified VIP: their CHIP-8 code at 0x260 copies the changes into the interpreter, calls more machine code (02AC) and clears the screen, and the program proper starts at 0x2C0. Emulators can apply the patch instead of running its 1802 code: when 0x200 holds 1260 and 0x202-0x249 hold the patch, switch to 64x64 and continue at 0x260, or at 0x2C0 after the self-patching code; then treat 0230 as clearing the screen. Often called "Hires CHIP-8"; not to be confused with Tom Swan's 64x128 HI-RES CHIP-8 (1980).

program.title: Astro Dodge Hires
program.description: The 64x64 version of Astro Dodge: make your way through the asteroid field, scoring a point for each asteroid you dodge. Keys 2, 4, 6 and 8 move the ship; 5 starts the game.

program.title: Hires Maze
program.description: The 64x64 version of Maze: draws a random maze of diagonal lines across the whole screen.

program.title: Hires Particle Demo
program.description: The 64x64 version of zeroZshadow's particle demo. Works on real hardware as well as emulators.

program.title: Hires Sierpinski
program.description: The 64x64 version of the Sierpinski demo.

program.title: Hires Stars
program.description: The 64x64 version of the Stars demo.

program.title: Hires Test
program.description: Draws 16 squares down the diagonal of the 64x64 screen, to show that the mode works. It is the test program printed with the 2 Page Display article (VIPER volume 1 issue 3, p. 12), moved to 0x2C0 after the self-patching code. kripod/chip8-roms credits it to Tom Swan (1979), who used the 2 Page Display in his book PIPS for VIPs.

program.title: Hires Worm V4
program.description: The 64x64 port of SuperWorm V4, Martijn Wenting's update of RB's SUPER-CHIP game Worm3.

program.title: Trip8 Hires Demo
program.description: The 64x64 version of the Trip8 demo: an intro, 3D vector balls and four randomised dot effects.
